_comment: Source of truth for the bootstrap element HISTORY, read by tools/fleet-drift-report.py. Each element's 'since' is the bootstrap version (client/bootstrap.ps1 $script:BootstrapVersion) that introduced it. current_version must equal max(since) AND the $script:BootstrapVersion constant. When you add a bootstrap capability: add an element with since = the new version, bump current_version here, and bump $script:BootstrapVersion in bootstrap.ps1 to match (the report warns if they drift). The report reads each unit's C:\\MAST\\bootstrap-manifest.json (stamped at bootstrap time) and lists elements with since > the unit's stamped version as 'may need applying'. Every element also declares 'reassert', which says whether it may be run again on an ALREADY-PROVISIONED unit (see docs/decisions/2026-08-24-bootstrap-elements-declare-whether-they-may-be-re-run.md): 'routine' = safe to re-assert on every provisioning run; 'provider' = a provisioning provider already re-asserts it, named in 'provider' -- do NOT run bootstrap's copy again; 'on-demand' = capable of running remotely but never on a routine run, invoked explicitly for repair; 'console' = first-touch only, never remote. build-mast.ps1 fails the build if the field is missing or invalid.

elements.description: Sync the system clock before anything TLS-sensitive (public NTP, with an HTTP Date header fallback off-campus)
Assert Israel Standard Time WITH automatic DST. Units arrived on the right zone with DST auto-adjust disabled and ran an hour off in summer; one idempotent tzutil /s fixes both
Create local 'mast' admin account with the provisioning password
Winlogon AutoAdminLogon for headless unattended sign-in

Suppress the machine-wide Windows backup-reminder notification task. The per-user toast and content-delivery half moved to the desktop-appearance provider in #106; consumer cloud content is covered by telemetry-privacy-harden
Ensure IPv4 uses DHCP (the fleet identifies units by hostname)
WinRM over HTTP 5985 + Basic auth, firewall port open, network profile Private
Diagnostic data = Security; disable DiagTrack/dmwappushservice, advertising ID, activity feed, Cortana/web search

Regional format English (United States), system + per-user. CONSOLE ONLY: its Set-WinHomeLocation call activates a RunAs='Interactive User' COM server, which blocks for a 600 s timeout in Session 0 -- i.e. on every remote run -- and then succeeds anyway (#148)
Disable Windows Firewall on all profiles (units sit on an isolated VLAN)
Stop + disable non-essential vendor services (Spooler, Search, Intel LMS, vendor helpers)
Set LocalMachine ExecutionPolicy to RemoteSigned (was a printed manual step, skipped on mast04 and mast03 -- see #51)
Assert 64 GB RAM and a free drive letter D: before anything is changed (both are required by the imdisk 32 GB RAM-backed D: mount)
Treat D: held by the bootstrap medium itself as no conflict, and tell the operator at the end of the run to unplug it, so a forgotten drive does not take D: back on the next boot

Install OpenSSH from the bundled Win32-OpenSSH MSI instead of the OpenSSH.Server Features-on-Demand capability, which reported success before registering sshd and left units with no SSH server (#123); a missing sshd is now a run blocker rather than a warning

Read the BIOS power policy (Restore AC Power Loss and the APM wake sources) from the UEFI setup varstore and compare against server/data/firmware-baseline.json; a unit that would not power itself back on after a mains event gets a red banner and waits for the operator to acknowledge, then continues on its own -- provisioning cannot write BIOS setup, so this informs and never blocks. Result and acknowledgment are stamped into bootstrap-manifest.json
